text:
maya: Heads up — after the multiplexing canary (region eu-west) went to 20% we started seeing a spike in client reconnects for streaming routes. Not huge but correlated with the rollout window. :eyes:
liam: ack. is this only SSE or WS too?
maya: mostly SSE (streaming/text/event-stream). WS shows a small bump but negligible.
ashley: do we have the console trace for a sample session id? can we see routing + quota stamps?
maya: pasted one trace snippet below — prefixed with our route/lease headers. session id `s:6f1a`
```
145ms GET /v1/stream -> upstream-3 (mux=true) x-route: shard-17 x-lease: sticky-2026-03
-> server: 200
client: received partial chunk, then `ERR: heartbeat-miss` and reconnect
```
liam: heartbeat-miss how long was heartbeat interval on canary? we tweaked heartbeat to 15s for multiplex.
maya: 15s client heartbeat, server keepalive 10s, so client expects at most 30s before reconnect. The observed disconnects happen ~28-31s after last chunk.
sam: could be jitter from multiplex aggregation — if a multiplex worker is busy it delays ping processing and triggers client-side reconnects. any spikes in CPU on the mux pods?
maya: yes, there were brief CPU spikes matching the window. pods autoscaled but we had a cold-started worker on some shard groups.
ashley: if the server delays pongs, we should prefer server-side queued heartbeats or send an op-code to clients to extend grace window rather than let clients immediately reconnect. re: UX, console currently shows reconnect counts but not per-route multiplex flag. makes it hard to filter.
devex: +1 on console telemetry. We should tag streaming metrics with `mux=true/false` and `keepalive-ms` so the SLO dashboard can be split. I'll add a ticket.
liam: short-term mitigation: increase server keepalive to 25s or have the middleware emit a quick noop event when under backpressure. That avoids client reconnect storms while we fix autoscale.
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-0315-01 (mux-reconnects). Paging oncall.
sam: small experiment idea: for clients that support resume token, let them insert exponential backoff with small randomized jitter (300-1200ms). That drops thundering herd on server when many reconnect at same second.
maya: good. Also found a mismatch in our proxy: when a session falls back from SSE -> WS (due to intermediate proxy), we were not propagating `x-resume-id` header into the ws handshake, causing resume to be impossible and forcing full session re-init (billing + state loss).
ashley: ouch. That explains duplicate charges seen in the console (2x token counts for same user).
devex: can we add a console annotation/alert when a resume fails server-side? currently it's buried in raw logs.
liam: quick fix: proxy patch to copy `x-resume-id` into `sec-websocket-protocol` token or a `x-resume-id` header during handshake. Longer fix: normalize resume semantics across SSE/WS in the routing layer.
maya: I'll open a PR for the proxy patch. Can someone own dashboard split + tagging for mux vs non-mux? it's blocking root cause triage for product.
devex: I'll own dashboard tagging. Will add `stream.mux`, `stream.keepalive_ms`, `route.shard` tags and a small console filter. ETA end of day.
sam: for rollout plan: pause further canary expansion until we verify keepalive change + proxy resume patch. Also add a canary-watch alert for reconnect-rate-per-route > 3x baseline.
ashley: agree. Also add a billing guard to detect duplicate token consumption on resume-fail patterns.
liam: quick note: include a low-frequency sampled trace for the next hour with full headers to help confirm header propagation. sample rate 1/1000 should be fine.
maya: thanks all — I'm doing the proxy PR now and will coordinate the canary hold. if we still see reconnects after keepalive bump we'll consider lowering mux concurrency per worker. :thumbsup:
